content:
Phase 68b implemented at c791854 (d17f404 implementation, 3348f4e tests + two fixes they found, c791854 docs). gate: see entry @ c791854. Details, deviations, guard changes and a per-screenshot evidence table are in the phase doc's 'Implementation notes'.

What / where (front end: tagteam/data/web/cockpit.{html,js,css})
- Turn blocks in both lanes: openBlock / foldBlock / applyBlockPolicy (newest open, earlier folded, a running block never folded by a refresh, the arbiter's own open/close kept); the lane (.timeline) is the one scroller — .act-lines in a lane has no max-height / overflow; BLOCK_CAP = 2000 for cycle, check and chat blocks with the note 'showing the last 2,000 lines [(the log may be longer)] — the whole log: <path>'; a fold bumps rec.gen so late SSE frames and late /api/tail responses are dropped; reopen = one consistent read.
- STREAMS (your approval note): a reopen never resets another consumer — if the key is registered the block is emptied and takes the registry's buffer replay from its start, else a fresh connection from 0 (a fold clears the cursor); conversation streams are filtered by turn; a REPLAYED end detaches the block without calling refreshAll again.
- Checks strip (#lane-checks, CHECKS store): gate / panel / panel_lens leave the reviewer's lane; a chip opens that run's block.
- Both lanes scoped to the cycle (LLANE through applyLaneScope; btn-lead-last). Backlog item closed in the roadmap.
- One story: laneText and the watcher-off / stalled / lost cards say n.headline; the new stalled/watcher-stale card opens the Phase 68 drawer; only inflight.liveness === 'lost' offers Cancel turn; 'pid_alive' no longer appears in cockpit.js (guarded).
- Chat turns are keyed blocks (buildMsgRow + a patching fillMsgRow, appendChatLine, chatLinesInto): 'you ▸ …' prompt, capped appended stream, reply / error as the closing line, continuity in the header; the signature no longer counts lines, so a poll never rebuilds the stream; an open block self-heals if its DOM and kept lines disagree.

Seen, not assumed (criterion 9): BEFORE the fix — a real 40 s pre-check showing 'gatekeeper's process disappeared mid-turn — Cancel turn' beside a bar saying 'Pre-check running' (payload pid None / pid_alive False / liveness no-child). After: the same situation with NO card and a running chip; reviewer and lead blocks streaming in a real headless cycle; the stalled trio (SIGSTOP-ped watcher) — bar, card with Open the watcher, and lane in one sentence; a real chat turn as a block.

The live look changed five things no green test had caught: (1) follow must be the reader's intent (LANE_FOLLOW, set only in the scroll handler; restick after opens/policy/chat renders) — judged by geometry, both lanes showed 'new output' to a reader who never scrolled; (2) the lead lane had three lines of output: the 'No messages yet' prompt now yields to turn blocks and the composer is one line until used; (3) the Start card offered the phase already running (a 68a consequence) — hidden while a turn is in flight or the headline is working/starting/launching; (4) SCOPE ADDITION, server side, one line: the rendered turn log ended '… cost=$0.81859325 …', now in full view, against the arbiter's standing no-API-dollars rule — headless.render_event no longer prints cost= (tokens/turns/duration stay; nothing stored changes; test against the real fixture); (5) stale 'streaming in the reviewer lane' wording for a pre-check. The Chromium test then found two more: trimming now loops to the cap, and the hold anchor is kept in whole pixels (17 px → 16 px drift across a trim).

Deviations: chat turns are scoped by the conversation picker, not folded by cycle time (the page has no cycle start time); a gate has no turn log so its block says so (showing the gate report would be a server change); the server-side change above.

Guards changed ON PURPOSE, none deleted: the lead block must not contain the <details> 'activity (N lines)' disclosure and must use the keyed stream + cap; the reviewer-lane test expects the pre-check in CHECKS as a chip (counts 5/3/2 → 5/2/2); the chat-merge test asserts prompt / stream / closing line and stream-node identity across a re-render; 'prompt stays with cards' is reversed and says why.

Tests: 13 node-harness tests (blocks, fold + late tail + late line, reopen clean read, reopen with the all-activity consumer attached, replayed end, caps for cycle and chat with the note, tail at exactly the cap, follow-as-intent + hold, anchor trimmed → oldest kept line, chat block patched not rebuilt, folded chat holds no DOM, lanes = headline with liveness deciding 'gone', checks routing + open/close) and 2 REAL-CHROMIUM tests with the shipped CSS and markup (a cycle block and a chat block: one scroller, follow, hold on a wrapped line, cap rollover while scrolled back, anchor trimmed, cue, a poll not moving the reader). Focused run of the eight front-end/API/headless files: 496 passed.

NOT seen (named in the doc): an earlier block folding as a new turn starts in the same cycle, the cue by hand, a bounced chip, turn-lost, the watcher-stale card, a block past 2,000 lines — node/Chromium tests only. The chat screenshot still shows cost= because that scratch server predated the renderer change (verified by its test only). No browser pass after the very last change (trim loop + whole-pixel anchor); the Chromium tests exercise exactly that.

GATE: PASS | scope 9 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2290 passed, 5 skipped, 7m47s)
checked: HEAD c791854

Reviewed c791854 against approved plan 1988723. Gate PASS at the same HEAD accepted: 2290 passed, 5 skipped. Reviewer focused run: tests/test_cockpit_activity.py + tests/test_headless.py, 221 passed (including real Chromium), 39.51s. git diff --check clean. No arbiter interjections. Owner-liveness and headline changes look correct; the small removal of rendered dollar cost is an acceptable documented scope addition.

Please fix:

1. Folding does not implement the promised single newest terminal block in the lead lane (cockpit.js foldChatBlock/buildMsgRow/fillMsgRow/applyChatPolicy and cockpit.css). foldChatBlock hides only rec.box; the full prompt and closing reply/error remain visible, with no CSS hiding them for a folded row. Using the shipped markup/CSS through _run_lanes_in_chromium, an automatically folded old chat with a 99-line reply is still 1957px tall and its reply has display:block. Also applyChatPolicy and applyBlockPolicy(LLANE) independently keep their newest block open: a finished chat remains open when a newer cycle turn starts. Use one chronological open/fold policy for the merged lead timeline, respecting explicit user choices and running blocks, and make a folded chat a one-line header with its prompt/reply/error preserved for reopening. Add real-layout coverage for a long finished chat followed by another chat and by a cycle turn. The conversation-picker scoping deviation need not require a new server API, but cannot leave these two separate newest-open policies.

2. Closing a running check is undone by the next activity refresh (upsertRow/openBlock/renderChecks). upsertRow unconditionally calls openBlock(rec,true) for every running item, including CHECKS, while toggleCheck's fold does not set userClosed. Reproduced with a running panel_lens: select chip, close chip => folded=true; upsert the same item + renderChecks + deliver a line => folded=false, CHECK_OPEN=null, one hidden stream DOM line. Thus closed/unselected checks keep streaming into hidden DOM, contrary to the approved folded-block guarantee. Gate opening by the selected check ID, detach/drop output for unselected checks, and fold the previously selected record when a cycle change clears CHECK_OPEN. Test close followed by multiple refreshes and late frames, selecting a different check, and cycle changes.

3. Complete the planned final browser pass after these fixes. The submission explicitly omits a pass after the final code change, and the missing live same-lane turnover is exactly where finding 1 escaped. Capture chat-to-cycle and successive same-lane turn transitions, check open/close across a refresh, and the current rendered output; keep unobserved states explicit. The isolated Chromium geometry tests remain useful but do not cover the full page lifecycle.

Nonblocking limitations to retain in the documentation: checks currently cannot display a gate report because gates have no turn log; a chip that says no log exists does not meet the original 'opens that run's log' criterion. Mark that criterion partial/deferred rather than calling this built as planned. The bounded in-memory chat retention differs from the plan's detach/re-read prescription, but can be acceptable if folding truly removes the body and reopening preserves the retained output without duplication.
